question: The arm's spread gate judges every name on the SIP spread from 16 minutes earlier (our plan's delay). If the desk ALSO checked the actual SIP spread at the moment it sends the order (refuse above 0.15%, unknown refuses), (A) would it keep losers out without costing profit, and (B) could the stale 16-minute pre-filter then be loosened to 0.25% to let more names (the open's movers whose spreads have since narrowed) in profitably? Upper bound for any live real-time spread source; it does not choose one.
operator_sentence: Operator 2026-10-30 ~04:45 ET in chat, after move_to_cost_hist came back NOT SUPPORTED (the LOW gap was the spread itself): 'If we have an answer to keep out the losers, let's go with that.' Queue order (operator 10/29 'Yes, swap them'): the order-time spread check before open_spread.
registered_at: 2026-10-30 ~05:00 ET, before any variant is built, run or read.
origin: running_list rows 34 and 39. ALGM 10/28 13:15 filled at the SIP ask on a 0.20% spread that the 16-minute-old 0.15% gate could not see. 10/27-10/28 live: 4 of 44 entries had an actual entry spread > 0.15% (AMKR, BROS, AAOI, ALGM), mean -14.4 bp; the other 40 -0.4 bp. 10/29 09:42: movers' delayed readings kept them out until ~10:00 after their spreads had narrowed. move_to_cost_hist (10/30, 96 historical sessions): removing the widest-spread events beat every other removal; mid-to-mid moves did not differ by range-to-spread.
contamination: 10/27 is a stage-1 session and its entry spreads were looked at (the 4-of-44 count above). Declared; the verdict must also hold with 10/27 removed (pass condition below).
prior: For (A): cost is the spread (fills at the touch), and wide-at-the-order entries lost in the small live sample. Against: those are 4 trades; an order-time refusal can also refuse a name whose spread is wide because it is moving. For (B): delayed readings misjudge names whose spreads move. Against: earlier studies found loosened spread gates admit losers (spread_gate 10/1: refused squares -0.93/-0.81% vs -0.15%). Prior lift (A) 0..+3 bp per trade, (B) -4..+4 bp.

knobs.ai_watch_order_spread_max_pct: NEW, default 0 (off = live unchanged). REPLAY-ONLY: when > 0, immediately before placing an order the desk reads the full SIP spread of the LAST usable quote stamped <= the order second (bid > 0, ask > bid, age <= 15 s) in % of mid; above the cap, or no usable quote, the order is not sent and the check is refused with code order_spread_wide / order_spread_unknown (counted outside the paint). Pure: its own cache keyed sym|int(ts); never writes _SIP_SPREAD_CACHE or the recorded inputs (test). The runner refuses to start if the knob is non-zero in config/bot_config.json: live has no real-time SIP.
knobs.ai_watch_order_spread_rand_block_share /: NEW, default 0 / ''. Control: at the same point, an order that would be sent is refused when sha256(salt|symbol|day|floor(ts/30)) < share (counted os2_counts.blocked_rand; the variant's refusals are os2_counts.blocked_variant).
knobs.ai_watch_max_sip_spread_pct (existing): The 16-minute-delayed arm gate cap, 0.15 live; varied to 0.25 / 0.30 in B variants only.
knobs.ai_watch_order_spread_rand_release_share: NEW, default 0 / ''. Control for B: an arm check refused spread_wide on the delayed reading at the LIVE cap 0.15% is released when sha256(salt|symbol|day|floor(ts/30)) < share (counted released_rand; the B variant's releases, delayed reading in (0.15, cap], are released_variant).

variants.REF: The square_relax REF desk under its amended_harness_switch (late_gates harness, 'src' staleness, slope-now OFF, arm_max_age 0), order-time check off.
variants.RAND_A_k (k=1,2,3): REF + random order-time block, salt 'OS2A-k', share calibrated per session so the seed-averaged blocked orders are within +-10% of OT15's blocked orders (bisection, <= 4 passes, seeds in parallel). Unmatched session = no lift_rand (counted).
variants.RAND_B_k (k=1,2,3): OT15 + random release of delayed spread_wide refusals at 0.15%, salt 'OS2B-k', matched by count to OT15_PRE25's released checks (+-10%, same bisection). The order-time check stays on in RAND_B, so both arms face the same final filter.
variants.MDE1: REF + random order-time block share 0.25, salt 'OS2-MDE'.
variants.REF_DUP: REF twice on the first, middle and last session (determinism).

fidelity_gate: This study runs only if square_relax's 2026-10-27 REF fidelity (amended_harness_switch, unchanged gate) PASSES: same harness, same pins. Its own check, required: on 2026-10-27, 20 OT15 order-time reads sampled at random (seed 'OS2-FID') equal a direct pull of the last SIP quote <= ts within 0.01 points; and a test shows a fetch for ts+100 never serves a read at ts. Fail = NOT TESTABLE.
harness: tools/replay_session.py via the square_relax runner's FLAGS/PIN (late_gates harness), one pinned --sha containing the knobs. Outputs ~/replay_runs/order_spread/DAY-VAR.json. Pricing as stale_age_read / open_spread: entry at the first SIP trade within 60 s of the replayed decision; the FULL SIP quoted spread at that entry is charged; open_at_end marked at the SIP 15:49 close; failed fetch = session not scored; > 10% no-print = excluded.
screen_first: Stage 1 = the 22 recorded sessions 2026-09-28..2026-10-27 split by count in date order, EARLY (first 11) and LATE (last 11). SCREEN FAIL / UNDERPOWERED / CONTROL UNMATCHED stops the study for that primary; nothing is switched on. SCREEN PASS runs stage 2: >= 10 forward recorded sessions, same rule over the forward block (halves by count), with stage2_monitoring.
statistic: Per session, per arm vs its comparator (A: OT15 vs REF and vs RAND_A; B: OT15_PRE25 vs OT15 and vs RAND_B): lift = mean net(variant) - mean net(comparator), bp per trade; session_lift = sum net(variant) - sum net(comparator), bp per session at equal size. REFUSED trades (A) = comparator trades with no variant match (same symbol, entry within 600 s); ADDED trades (B) = variant trades with no comparator match. Sessions equal-weighted, day-clustered (std_scorer.day_stat), one-sided bounds at 0.975, t at n-1 df.

pass.A_OT15: PASSES the screen only if ALL: (1) PRIMARY: refused-trade net (REF trades OT15 refused) minus RAND_A refused-trade net (seed-averaged), per session: point estimate < 0 in BOTH halves and upper one-sided bound <= +5 bp over all scored sessions (refusals pick worse trades than random refusals); (2) session_lift(OT15 - REF) point estimate >= 0 in BOTH halves (keeping losers out does not lose money); (3) HARM: whole-session per-trade lift(OT15 - REF) lower bound >= -2 bp (operator's '2 bp + average >= 0'; REF_DUP difference > 1 bp raises the 2 bp by that amount) and point >= 0; (4) (1)-(3) point estimates keep their signs with 2026-10-27 removed; (5) >= 30 refused trades in all and >= 6 sessions with refusals in each half, else UNDERPOWERED.
pass.B_OT15_PRE25: Scored ONLY if A passes (fixed sequence; no alpha spent otherwise). PASSES only if ALL: (1) PRIMARY: added-trade net (OT15_PRE25 trades with no OT15 match) minus RAND_B added-trade net (seed-averaged), per session: point >= 0 in BOTH halves and lower bound >= -5 bp over all sessions; (2) session_lift(OT15_PRE25 - OT15) point >= 0 in BOTH halves; (3) HARM: per-trade lift lower bound >= -2 bp (+ REF_DUP penalty) and point >= 0; (4) OT15_PRE25 opens more trades than OT15 before 10:00 ET (it actually brings the movers in); (5) >= 30 added trades and >= 6 sessions with added trades per half, else UNDERPOWERED.

power: MDE per half = 3.08 x sd_session / sqrt(sessions) with sd_session = sd across sessions of (RAND_1 - mean(RAND_2, RAND_3)) on the primary's refused (A) / added (B) net x sqrt(3/2); <= 6 bp per half, else UNDERPOWERED. A count-only pass runs first (counts and MDE, no means); if the projected refused or added count is < 30, stop. Declared likely thin for A: ~4 of 44 live entries were wide at the order over two days.
fail: Powered and any condition missed: FAIL; live unchanged. Report FAIL (point estimate wrong sign) separately from FAIL (bound only), the second recorded as 'not shown', not 'refuted'.
if_pass: result-skeptic Mode 3 on the result. Then a separate operator decision on the LIVE source, each with its own check before going live: (a) the free real-time IEX quote, calibrated against SIP on recorded days (IEX overstated 1.5-3.3x before; the cap would be re-expressed on IEX and re-checked), or (b) paid real-time SIP under the no-spend-until-proven rule. A pass is evidence the check is worth having; it switches nothing on.
stage2_monitoring: As square_relax: after each forward session STOP if the variant's trades < 70% of its comparator's (A) / not above (B), or that session's lift < -10 bp; from the 3rd forward session STOP if the cumulative lift's upper one-sided bound < 0. No early PASS.
information_only: OT15_PRE30 vs OT15 and vs OT15_PRE25.
Refused orders by spread band at the order (0.15-0.25, 0.25-0.50, > 0.50%) and by minute (09:30-10:00 vs later); unknown vs wide.
Added trades (B) by minute bucket and by delayed-reading band; names released per session.
Live cross-check: the same split (entry spread > 0.15% vs not) on live fills 10/28-forward, using Alpaca FILL activities and the SIP quote at the fill second.
no_retuning: No other order-time cap, pre-filter cap or quote-age rule is scored as primary.
multiplicity: Two primaries in fixed sequence: A at full alpha; B only after A passes.
script: Knobs (ai_entry_watch, default off), a pure order-time SIP read with tests (no look-ahead, no cache leak, runner refuses non-zero live config), tools/studies/order_spread_run.py (reusing square_relax_run / late_gates_run, parallel control seeds) and order_spread_read.py (stale_age_read pricing, square_relax_read screen/stage-2 checks), written after a result-skeptic READY; they may not change anything above. Runs after square_relax in the after-hours queue, one batch at a time.
